content.text:

segments.text: A winter 2026 knee flare increased oral ibuprofen exposure; by April 21, pain had settled, she reported topical-gel use and ibuprofen only twice in the preceding month, and BP improved to 126/76 and 124/74 on the last documented regimen of diltiazem ER 240 mg daily and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.

content.text: Two-month recheck arranged at her February visit, following a winter flare of knee pain during which her oral ibuprofen use had increased and both her blood pressure and creatinine had drifted marginally upward.

segments.text: Osteopenia was managed with calcium and vitamin D, with repeat DXA planned for 2027; A1c was 5.8% in September 2025, and the latest reviewed LDL was 146 mg/dL in August 2024 without an identified active lipid-lowering prescription.

content.text:
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Essential hypertension at goal on diltiazem and hydrochlorothiazide.
2. Hyperlipidemia — low-density lipoprotein 146, stable over thirteen years of measurement. Dietary discussion repeated.
3. Abnormal glucose 5.8, drifting slightly. Continue current activity, recheck annually.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Pneumococcal vaccination — she now meets the age threshold and the vaccine was given today, nine years after infectious diseases first raised it during her 2016 pneumonia admission. She was pleased that it had been tracked. This is worth recording plainly: she had bacteraemic pneumococcal pneumonia at 55 and has been unprotected …
